text.p: Gold prices continued their rebound with a strong close on Friday. COMEX August gold contract has risen nearly $12 since Wednesday. Wheat, sugar and base metals all rose on Friday, while oil prices ended lower.
The CRB index rose 0.85 points to 235.04.

GOLD - COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended sharply higher for the second day in a row Friday, led by heavy fund shortcovering in gold. "The slump in the stock market Friday might be used as an excuse for gold's recovery, but really it was just that funds are taking the opportunity to cover their
large short positions, plus there's been some producers (who) have been lifting hedges this week," Merrill Lynch commodity research director, Bill O'Neill, said.
"However, our view is that this is a natural trading turn in the market, but may not be a major trend change, and the 12 year lows seen last week may yet be revisited," he said.

COMEX August gold ended up $4.90 an ounce at $329.60, after seeing an eleven day high at $330.90 intraday. COMEX gold total volume was estimated at a heavy 55,000 lots, with traders reporting 3,000 lots of exchange-for-physicals done as well.
The move followed a $6.00 jump in August gold on Thursday.

METALS - Copper and aluminium prices led other metals higher during a more active Friday LME session, and both closed firm around the days highs. Traders said gains in these two, and elsewhere in the complex, reflected end-week position squaring. In copper, also, the spreads were widening out during the afternoon session. "The market still remains tight...it (the stock increases) is only metal lent to the market," analyst Martin Squires of LME trader Rudolf Wolff and Co said.

LME stocks rose again on Friday, up 7,800 tonnes to 181,150 tonnes. The total inventory increase in copper this week has been 42,025 tonnes in reaction to the well-heralded technical squeeze. The cash/threes spread moved out to $138/148 backwardation this afternoon, having traded at $120 during the morning. Cash/one day was at $20 backwardation.
Three months prices broke above $2,300, and by the end of the kerb were at $2,316, up $36 a tonne from Thursday.
Aluminium did not really react to a 2,550-tonne stock fall, although the decline this week has been 9,175 tonnes.
Nevertheless, prices eventually moved higher, with a technical break above $1,585 helping to trigger some commission house buying, Squires noted.
The $1,600 level was achieved and maintained on the kerb, and last trade was at $1,607.50, up $28.50.
Zinc reached up and hit a fresh 6-3/4 year high of $1,534 a tonne at one stage, maintaining the current strong uptrend.
In the short-term, with September tightness looming, there is little downside scope, analysts said.
Nickel prices again fell away during the kerb session, with the market unable to sustain a mid-afternoon rally.
Traders said that despite Friday's stock fall, the general inventory trend remains upwards with ample Russian metal available. Last trade was at $6,740, down $90 from Thursday.
Lead traded steadily throughout the session, and showed signs of regaining poise after the mid-week sell-off. Last trade was at $648, up $7.
Tin managed technical consolidation as well after dropping to 2-1/3 year lows this week, although the extent of the rally was fairly limited. Last business was at $5,460, up $20.
Alloy was generally quiet, but was marked up on the kerb to finish at a higher $1,442/45 a tonne.

GRAINS - CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on gains in corn and soybeans. Concerns about renewed forecasts for drier weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest corn/soybean growing region led to the surge in corn and bean futures, traders said. "Wheat is going along for the ride right now," a trader said. Gains in wheat continued to be checked by a large U.S. hard red winter wheat crop being harvested this year in the U.S. Great Plains and in the eastern U.S. soft red winter region.

OIL - NYMEX oil prices fell sharply Friday as fears that a hurricane would disrupt refinery operations faded just when the oil complex was poised to consolidate anyway. August crude settled off 72 cents at $19.27 a barrel. August heating oil ended off 1.67 cents at 52.22 cents a gallon while August gasoline finished 1.84 cents a gallon lower at 60.05 cents.

SUGAR - CSCE world sugar futures closed firmer and over key resistance, suggesting that follow-through fund buying on Monday could fuel the benchmark October contract toward its next upside target. Steady producer selling coupled with light local

liquidation kept the contract close to unchanged for most of the day. The October contract ended 0.12 cent higher at 11.28 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.29 to 11.16 cents. Second-position March also settled 0.12 cent firmer at 11.47. Several of the deferred months climbed to new, life-of-contract highs during the session.
